name: Do I need a permit to replace a bathroom vanity in San Diego or Chula Vista?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to replace a bathroom vanity in San Diego or Chula Vista?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A vanity replacement may require plumbing or electrical review when fixtures, drains, outlets, or lighting are added, moved, or substantially altered. A same-place, like-for-like replacement may be treated differently, but local requirements depend on the exact work and jurisdiction.

Context: The City of San Diego’s published guidance distinguishes maintenance-like replacements from work that changes plumbing fixtures or other building systems. Elite Remodeling & Design can identify the project scope and coordinate permit-related steps when the vanity is part of a permitted bathroom remodel.

Key factors:
- Whether water or drain lines move
- Whether an outlet or lighting changes
- Whether walls are opened
- Which city has jurisdiction over the property

Practical guidance: Ask for a written scope showing who determines permit needs and who handles applications, inspections, and closeout. Do not assume a cabinet replacement has the same requirements as a layout change.

Early scope review is especially useful in San Diego County communities with different permitting offices.
acceptedAnswer.description: Possibly. A same-place replacement may differ from work that moves plumbing, changes electrical fixtures, opens walls, or alters the layout. San Diego guidance treats plumbing and electrical changes differently from certain like-for-like maintenance work, so confirm the exact scope before starting.
